kosten.et: From Old High German kostōn, from Proto-Germanic *kustōną. More at costen.

Kost.et: From Middle High German kost(e), from Old High German kosta, deverbal from kostōn (“to try, to taste”).

Kosten.et:
From Middle High German koste, kost. From Medieval Latin costus, costa. Ultimately from the Latin verb constare.
Older singular forms were found in Kost f, Koste f, Kost m, and Kosten m.

s: skirt suit (women’s business suit consisting of a skirt and jacket)
costume, fancy dress (outfit worn for masquerade)

Kostüm.et: First borrowed in the early 18th century directly from Italian costume, which see. Later influenced by French costume, itself also from the Italian.

s: cosmetics (act or study of enhancing beauty)

köstlich.et: From Middle High German kostlich, kostelich. By surface analysis, kosten (“to taste”) + -lich.

koscher.et: Borrowed from Yiddish כּשר (kosher), from Hebrew כָּשֵׁר (kašér).

Kosmopolit.et: From Ancient Greek κοσμοπολίτης (kosmopolítēs, “citizen of the world”) (κόσμος (kósmos, “world”) + πολίτης (polítēs, “citizen”)).
